children: said it is unable to restore access to its cloud computing facility in Bahrain and one of its data-hosting zones in the United Arab Emirates more than six months after they were struck by Iranian drones.

"The damage to our infrastructure spanned multiple Availability Zones and exceeded what our regional and multi-AZ services are designed to withstand," AWS wrote in a status update about its Bahrain facility. Availability zones refer to groups of data ​centers in the same region.
"After a thorough assessment, we have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively in this Region," it added.
AWS said it remains committed to supporting its customers in Bahrain in the long term and will share a further update early next year.

In the UAE, AWS said ​it is unable to restore access to resources and data hosted exclusively in one Availability Zone. "We are working on replacing the affected infrastructure and will provide an update on the restoration of our services in the coming months."
AWS' customers in the affected areas have migrated their workloads to other regions, using backups where available.

title: AWS unable to restore service to Bahrain, UAE facilities after Iran strikes
